page: Amazon Web Services m7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor with 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it features x86_64 architecture and includes 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 25%. Text processing and small-model LLM inference text generation are highly efficient, with the latter reaching top-tier status in the top 10% at 338.71 tokens per second. Multi-core operations, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the average tier, indicating stable, predictable performance across general workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7a.4xlarge offers a modern DDR5 memory subsystem and dedicated physical cores without the overhead of hyperthreading, providing reliable resource density for general-purpose enterprise applications. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs limits its suitability for high-I/O databases or heavy machine learning training. It is best suited for web serving, software compilation, text processing, and running small-scale language model inference.
